summary: The Strategy pattern passes the rule for a task into an object instead of writing every rule inside it. In JavaScript, a strategy is usually just a function.
notes: new Gradebook(dropLowest) passes the function itself. Writing dropLowest() would call it and pass the result.
strategy.name is the function's name as a string, used here to label each line.
book.strategy = dropLowest swaps the rule on an existing object without changing the Gradebook class.
pitfall: Writing new Gradebook(dropLowest()) calls the function with no argument, so scores is undefined and it fails with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length').
contrast: JavaScript passes plain functions as strategies, like Python. Java needs an interface for the strategy, which a lambda or method reference then fills in.
